title: Lessons, Grover's band and playing at Tom Anderson's
summary: Brunies mentions a few lessons from Johnny DeDroit and an old trombonist, then the band with Grover, his wife and others at Tom Anderson's place near Canal and Rampart, where he stayed while Armstrong went north.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Did you ever play with them? No. Johnny played Trump. Johnny played Trump. Johnny played Trump. I took a couple lessons from Johnny, but I didn't like it. I figured it would come out of my head. He was better than sitting down with music. Yeah. Yeah. He's one of our old neighbors, Johnny Deetra. Yeah, Johnny Deetra. Is that right? That's right. Wonderful people. An old man used to tell me, you're going to regret it. You're going to regret it. I said, no, I ain't. I said, what comes out that head is good, and it's good and hot. I said, ain't no marches. Richie, what was the name of the old fella? I worked out for Grover, and he played. He was trying to give me trombone lessons. He worked for Grover out there. He was an old trombone player. Oh, Ricky Tom? Ricky Tom. He told me. Rock hitters, you never learn how to read a note. Then I used to play out at Anderson. I was a white trumpet player. I didn't play either. In Anderson. It was Louis Armstrong playing that first. George is the one that. Tom Anderson at the Rampart and Canal.

So it was Grover, his wife, his brother-in-law, and Ricky Tomes, and myself, and August Shillain. He's there, three, three, three, not so long ago. And we used to play at Anderson. Some Anderson. And they did away with Armstrong. Armstrong went up north and did good. Yeah. And I stayed down there and did bad.
Oh, well, maybe you had a good time, too, here.
I think my family was too big and I didn't want to travel.
